newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska cattle market quiet, no trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska cattle market quiet, no trade - feedlots.

text.p: Weather forecasters continued to call for extreme cold and brutal wind chills this week in the U.S. Plains, which has feedlots in Nebraska trimming showlists and raising asking prices, market sources there said.

Owners were asking $109.00 to $110.00 per cwt but packer inquiry was spotty at $108.00. No sales were reported Monday morning. Cattle last week sold from $106.00 to $109.00, with most at $108.00-$109.00 on volume, USDA confirmed.
The state's showlist this week was estimated at 78,000 head, down 10,000 from last week.
